policy: An injury is compensable under workers' compensation only if it arises out of and in the course of employment. Injuries sustained during the employee's normal commute between home and the regular workplace do not arise in the course of employment and are not compensable.
scenario: Dana is a payroll clerk who works fixed hours at the company's downtown office. One morning, while driving her own car along her usual route from home to that office, she was rear-ended at a stoplight and suffered whiplash. She had no work errand to run and was carrying no work equipment.
question: Is Dana's whiplash injury compensable under workers' compensation?
